beats.say: A fake email is often followed by a call. The caller claims to be an investigator or a prosecutor.
Even an official looking number on the screen can be fake. Callers can change the number shown.
Real law enforcement never asks for money, card details or an SMS code by phone.
Hang up, find the agency's official number yourself and tell your security team.

scenes.title: An investigator calls
scenes.intro: A fake notice arrived this morning, now someone calls. Read what they say and choose your answer.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering is not dangerous. What matters is what you do next.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That works too. If you are worried, call the agency's official number yourself.

steps.say: This is investigator Elçin Həsənov, Central Investigation Bureau. You ignored this morning's notice, and your name appears in a criminal case.
steps.spoken: <breath> This is investigator Elçin Həsənov, Central Investigation Bureau. You ignored this morning's notice, uh, and your name appears in a criminal case.

actions.label: What should I do? Tell me
actions.feedback: Going along with fear hands control to the caller. Check who they are first.

actions.label: I will call the bureau's official number myself
actions.feedback: Right. A real investigator will not object to you checking.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Good decision. You do not have to respond to a threat by phone.

steps.say: I am putting you through to the prosecutor. This is prosecutor Tofiq Abbasov. To protect your savings, move them to a safe account during the check.
steps.spoken: I am putting you through to the prosecutor. This is prosecutor Tofiq Abbasov. To protect your savings, <breath> move them to a safe account during the check.

actions.label: Give me the account, I will transfer
actions.feedback: The "safe account" belongs to the scammer. If you transferred money, call your bank now.

actions.label: I do not move money over the phone
actions.feedback: Right. No prosecutor asks you to move money to another account by phone.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. Passing you to a "senior official" is meant to raise the pressure.

steps.say: This is a secret investigation. If you tell your manager or family, you will be held responsible.
steps.spoken: This is a secret investigation. If you tell your manager or family, <breath> you will be held responsible.

actions.label: All right, I will tell no one
actions.feedback: A demand for secrecy cuts you off from help. Speak up at once instead.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. "Do not tell anyone" is the clearest sign of fraud.

steps.say: One last step. Tell me the code that just arrived on your phone so we can register you in the system.
steps.spoken: <breath> One last step. Tell me the code that just arrived on your phone so we can register you in the system.

actions.label: I read out the code
actions.feedback: The code is a key to your account or a payment. Once you say it, you lose control.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Right. No agency asks for an SMS code by phone.

steps.label: The call has ended. What now?

actions.label: Call the number on the bureau's official website
actions.feedback: Right. If you can, use another phone so the line cannot be kept open.

actions.label: Tell your manager and the security team
actions.feedback: Well done. A report protects your colleagues from the same call.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The scammer will call again. Reporting protects you and your colleagues.

scenes.prompt: Is this message safe or a scam?

messages.text: Central Investigation Bureau: transfer your fine to this card within 2 hours: 4169 **** 7731

cards.explain: Law enforcement does not collect fines to a personal card. Report this message.

body.text: An official letter from the court has arrived in your name. You can collect it from the registry office against signature.

cards.explain: The letter came through the institution's own channel and asks for no money or link.

body.text: Switch to a video call and show your ID card to the camera, we are running a check.

cards.explain: An image of your ID can be used to open fake accounts in your name. Such checks are not done by messenger.

artifact.label: Demands you move money to a "safe account"

cards.explain: There is no "safe account". It belongs to the scammer.

body.text: There is a new letter in your personal account.

cards.explain: No payment and no link. You open the portal yourself to read it.

scenes.prompt: Put the steps after a fake "prosecutor" call in order.

items.label: Write down the number, the time and what was said
Find the agency's official number yourself and check
Tell your manager and the security team

scenes.explain: If you transferred money, call your bank first. Your notes help the security team trace the attack.

question.prompt: The caller says: "This is a secret investigation, tell no one." What does it mean?

options.label: It is serious, I must keep quiet
options.feedback: Silence is what the scammer wants. If you speak up, the trick is exposed quickly.

options.label: They want to keep me from getting help
options.feedback: Right. That is exactly why you tell your manager and the security team at once.

options.label: I will tell only my family
options.feedback: Telling family is good, but the security team should also know about a work related call.

scenes.explain: Secrecy, threats and a money demand together are a known fraud pattern.

points: An official number on screen can be fake: hang up and check yourself.
Law enforcement never asks for money, card details or codes by phone.
If told "tell no one", tell the security team at once.
